sources.title: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts, Numerical Methods, Meteorological Training Course Lecture Series, 2002
sources.locator: Complete 98-page lecture-note PDF inspected. Read Chapter 5 §§5.1–5.2 (printed pp. 49–51), §5.5's interpolation conventions (printed pp. 52–55), and §5.7 on trajectory computation (printed pp. 56–58).
sources.reading_status: The full-text PDF was opened and the complete relevant semi-Lagrangian sections were read. Section 5.1 derives the characteristic/departure-point update and interpolation step; §5.2 analyzes the linear interpolation stability factor; §5.7 describes iterative trajectory computation and explicitly notes that its three-iteration practice has no convergence test.
sources.support: Supports the method's departure-point/backtracking organization and the need to distinguish interpolation stability from trajectory accuracy. The batch supplies independent convex-weight, local-foot, and global-error proofs; the source is not a substitute for those proofs.

contents.name: Characteristic conservation and backtracking from a regular arrival grid to a departure point, followed by interpolation
contents.detail: The algorithm follows this structure and fixes a periodic tensor grid and explicit Euler foot. Its exact procedure and status rules are stated locally.

contents.name: One-dimensional linear-interpolation stability analysis
contents.detail: The source's Fourier calculation is context. The local proof establishes the stronger sup-norm contraction directly from nonnegative tensor weights summing to one.

contents.name: Iterative departure-point computation with a fixed three-iteration practice and no convergence test
contents.reason: The authored method uses one explicit Euler backward step with a proved O(dt^2) local defect; it does not use or claim convergence of a fixed-iteration implicit trajectory solve.

contents.name: Cubic, quasi-monotone, spherical, and coupled atmospheric model branches
contents.reason: The assigned theorem is the periodic scalar linear-transport branch with tensor multilinear interpolation; no higher-order limiter, spherical coordinate, or coupled-equation claim is made.

sources.title: Lukas Einkemmer and Alexander Ostermann, On the error propagation of semi-Lagrange and Fourier methods for advection problems, Computers & Mathematics with Applications 69 (2015), 170–179
sources.locator: Full-text article inspected. §2.1 describes the semi-Lagrangian update and worst-case error growth with the number of steps; §4 derives the mean interpolation error and contrasts local conservation; §7 summarizes the limits of that error-growth observation. The one-dimensional model uses periodic boundary conditions.
sources.reading_status: The complete full-text article was opened and inspected. The full reasoning in §§2.1 and 4 was read, including the single-step interpolation formula, error accumulation argument, cell-averaged linear-interpolation calculation, and contrast with the conservative discontinuous-Galerkin reconstruction.
sources.support: Supports the repeated-projection error mechanism, the fact that higher spatial accuracy does not itself remove per-step error accumulation, and the warning that pointwise semi-Lagrangian interpolation is not generally conservative. The article's particular q convention and constant-velocity setting are not imported as the local theorem's hypotheses.

contents.name: A departure-point update requires interpolation because the foot need not be a grid node
contents.detail: The local algorithm states this update for a time-dependent velocity and a periodic tensor grid.

contents.name: Worst-case error contribution accumulates with the number of time steps, while exact characteristics remove the temporal foot error
contents.detail: The source motivates the count of repeated local defects. The local proof separately tracks foot error O(dt^(q+1)) and interpolation error O(h^(r+1)), then sums the recurrence.

contents.name: Linear interpolation need not conserve the spatial mean; conservative cellwise reconstruction is a separate method
contents.detail: The source supplies the warning only. The example gives a separate exact three-node smooth-velocity witness; the A-page overlap remap has its own mass/positivity argument.

contents.name: The discontinuous-Galerkin conservative semi-Lagrangian method and its multi-coefficient state
contents.reason: The conservative branch here is the distinct exact characteristic-cell overlap transfer specified in the plan; no DG cell-polynomial scheme is claimed.
